description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing and shows the expected-containers list it would create; apply adds log rotation and build-cache limits to daemon.json without disturbing the keys already there, writes a file dockerd accepts, creates the list once, from every container present, marks it not reviewed, and never rewrites it, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. Before the list is reviewed, a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image. After review, it removes an old stopped container that nothing protects, and keeps, with their images, stopped containers that are on the list, have an unless-stopped policy, or are labelled tc.keep. With Docker restarted under extra daemon flags each time: a --log-driver=journald daemon and a --log-opt daemon get no log-opts in daemon.json and still start; a --log-driver=json-file daemon gets them and starts with them; a stopped daemon's flags are read from docker.service and its environment file, and flags it cannot resolve skip log rotation with exit 3; a daemon.json an earlier version already broke is reported as DAEMON WILL NOT START, exit 3, unchanged, and Docker really does fail to start with it. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. Restarting Docker to load the new settings, and a host without Docker, are Tier 2. A container label is untrusted: one whose Compose project label carries a forged row cannot add a row or a field to the container listing, so a reviewed prune keeps the listed stopped container the forged row named, names the containers whose labels cannot be read, keeps them, and never prints the label; a new list leaves them off and says so. When docker ps fails but docker info answers (a shim on PATH), the prune prints ERROR, exits 1 and removes nothing, not even a network; Prune now exits 1; and the list is not created, exit 3. Writing daemon.json: the new file is made in the directory of the real target and renamed into place, so it keeps the mode, owner and group of the file it replaces (a 0600 file holding a fake proxy credential stays 0600 with its non-root group; a new file is 0644 root:root) and a symlinked daemon.json stays a symlink while its target changes and Docker restarts with it; a dangling symlink, or a link to a directory, is refused with exit 3 and nothing is created; after a successful Apply, a failed validation and Report mode, no .daemon.json.tc-* file is left in /etc/docker, and one left by a crashed earlier run is removed; Report mode on a host with no /etc/docker does not create it; seven changes in a row leave the newest five backups; and an immutable daemon.json makes the run exit 1 with the file byte-for-byte unchanged, no staging file and no backup.

steps.label: Record daemon.json as it was before the component
steps.run: mkdir -p /etc/docker; if [ -s /etc/docker/daemon.json ]; then cp /etc/docker/daemon.json /tmp/tc-before.json; else echo '{}' > /tmp/tc-before.json; fi; cat /tmp/tc-before.json

steps.label: Report mode
Report mode changed nothing
steps.run: test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/tc-docker-prune.timer && test ! -e /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers && { cmp -s /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json || { test ! -s /etc/docker/daemon.json && test "$(cat /tmp/tc-before.json)" = '{}'; }; }

steps.label: Apply
daemon.json carries the limits
Every key that was already there is unchanged
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; a=json.load(open('/tmp/tc-before.json')); b=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); bad=[k for k in a if b.get(k)!=a[k] and k not in ('log-opts','builder')]; print('changed:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

steps.label: dockerd accepts the new file
steps.run: dockerd --validate --config-file /etc/docker/daemon.json

steps.label: Prune timer enabled and scheduled
steps.run: systemctl is-enabled tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl is-active tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl list-timers tc-docker-prune.timer --no-pager

steps.label: Prune script has an age filter and never prunes volumes
Prune script carries one TC_PRUNE_VERSION stamp, a whole number, near the top
steps.run: f=/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune; n=$(grep -c '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=' $f); first=$(grep -n '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=' $f | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f1); echo "stamp lines: $n, first at line $first"; grep '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=' $f; [ "$n" = 1 ] && [ "$first" -le 10 ] && grep -qE '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=[0-9]+$' $f

steps.label: The stamp equals the version in component.json
steps.run: m=Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/component.json; [ -f "$m" ] || { echo "cannot find $m from $(pwd)"; exit 1; }; want=$(jq -r '.general.version' "$m"); have=$(sed -n 's/^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=\([0-9][0-9]*\)$/\1/p' /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune); echo "component.json version: $want; installed stamp: $have"; [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$have" ]

steps.label: Second run changes nothing
One-off prune, before review: no containers or images touched
A run of the prune prints its version as its first line
steps.run: m=Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/component.json; want=$(jq -r '.general.version' "$m"); out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; first=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 1); echo "first line: $first (exit $rc)"; [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ "$first" = "tc-docker-prune version $want" ]

steps.label: The prune service itself runs
steps.run: systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service && systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value

steps.label: The timer's service puts the version in the journal
steps.run: want=$(jq -r '.general.version' Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/component.json); journalctl --sync >/dev/null 2>&1; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service --no-pager | grep "tc-docker-prune version $want"

steps.label: Expected list created, with its header
Ignore file created with an example
Settings file carries only the age
Stopped containers: one listed, one unless-stopped, one tc.keep, one unprotected
steps.run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $d/bin; cp /bin/sleep /bin/true $d/bin/; for l in $(ldd /bin/sleep | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p $d$(dirname $l); cp $l $d$l; done; for t in listed policy labelled junk; do tar -C $d -c . | docker import --change "LABEL tc.test=$t" - tc-test-$t:1; done; echo name:tc-listed >> /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers; docker create --name tc-listed tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true; docker run -d --name tc-policy --restart unless-stopped tc-test-policy:1 /bin/sleep 3600; docker stop -t 1 tc-policy; docker create --name tc-labelled --label tc.keep=true tc-test-labelled:1 /bin/true; docker create --name tc-junk tc-test-junk:1 /bin/true; docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}}' | grep tc-test; docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

steps.label: A later run never rewrites the list
The hand-added entry is still on the list
Before review: a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image
steps.run: sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune && systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service -n 40 --no-pager; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-junk; docker image inspect -f 'junk image survived' tc-test-junk:1

steps.run: echo 'tc-test review' > /etc/tc-docker/reviewed && cat /etc/tc-docker/reviewed

steps.label: A later run reports the list as reviewed
After review: prune with no age limit, run by the timer's service
steps.run: docker inspect -f 'before: {{.Name}} present' tc-junk; docker ps -a --format 'before: {{.Names}} {{.Status}}'; sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune && systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service -n 40 --no-pager; docker ps -a --format 'after: {{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

steps.run: for c in tc-listed tc-policy tc-labelled; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} kept' $c; done; for i in listed policy labelled; do docker image inspect -f "image tc-test-$i kept" tc-test-$i:1; done; docker inspect tc-junk >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'tc-junk STILL HERE' || echo 'tc-junk removed'; docker image inspect tc-test-junk:1 >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'junk image STILL HERE' || echo 'junk image removed'

Failing Docker: an unprotected stopped container and an unused network, which a working prune would remove; then a docker shim that fails docker ps
steps.run: set -e; docker create --name tc-shim-junk tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true >/dev/null; docker network create tc-shim-net >/dev/null; sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; set +e; real=$(command -v docker); test "$real" != /usr/local/sbin/docker || exit 1; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' '# tc-test shim: Docker answers everything except docker ps' '[ "$1" = ps ] && { echo "Error response from daemon: tc-test simulated failure" >&2; exit 1; }' "exec $real \"\$@\"" > /usr/local/sbin/docker; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/docker; hash -r; docker ps; echo "docker ps exit $?"; docker info --format 'docker info still answers: {{.ServerVersion}}'

steps.run: /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune; echo "prune exit $?"; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-shim-junk stopped-old; docker network inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-shim-net

steps.label: Refuses a bad log size
Refuses a prune age under 24 hours
Refuses a schedule systemd cannot parse
Daemon flags: set up a helper that restarts Docker with extra dockerd flags through a docker.service drop-in
steps.run: set -e; systemctl show docker.service -p ExecStart --value | sed -n 's/.*argv\[\]=\([^;]*\) ;.*/\1/p' | head -n 1 > /tmp/tc-execstart; test -s /tmp/tc-execstart; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# tc-test-docker-flags FLAG...: restart docker.service with these extra dockerd flags (a drop-in).' 'd=/etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d' 'mkdir -p "$d"' '{ echo "[Service]"; echo "EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/tc-test-docker"; echo "ExecStart="; echo "ExecStart=$(cat /tmp/tc-execstart) $*"; } > "$d/tc-test.conf"' 'systemctl daemon-reload' 'systemctl reset-failed docker.service docker.socket 2>/dev/null' 'if systemctl restart docker.service; then' '  for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done' '  echo "docker came up with [$*]: LoggingDriver=$(docker info --format "{{.LoggingDriver}}")"' 'else' '  echo "docker DID NOT START with [$*]"' '  journalctl -u docker.service -n 50 --no-pager | grep -E "failed to start|unable to configure|unknown log opt|specified both" | tail -n 3' '  exit 1' 'fi' > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-docker-flags; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-docker-flags; echo "docker.service starts: $(cat /tmp/tc-execstart)"

steps.label: daemon.json write: install a helper that runs the component several times inside one step
steps.run:
cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-run-component <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-run-component [VAR=value ...]: run the component body the way the harness does (root, clean environment, the script's own defaults), for a step that needs several runs. usrPruneSchedule is blank, so the timer is left alone: these steps are about daemon.json.
exec env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root usrPruneSchedule= "\$@" /bin/bash "$(pwd)/Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin.sh"
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-run-component; echo "helper runs: $(grep -c exec /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-run-component) exec line"

steps.label: daemon.json write: an existing daemon.json, 0600 with a non-root owner and group, holding a fake proxy credential
steps.run: getent group tc-test-grp >/dev/null || groupadd tc-test-grp; rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker; printf '%s\n' '{"proxies": {"http-proxy": "http://tc-test-user:tc-test-not-a-password@proxy.invalid:3128"}}' > /etc/docker/daemon.json; chown nobody:tc-test-grp /etc/docker/daemon.json; chmod 600 /etc/docker/daemon.json; echo "before: $(stat -c '%a %U %G' /etc/docker/daemon.json)"

steps.label: daemon.json write: seven changes in a row, each made by a run of the component
steps.run:
set -u
rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker
printf '{"debug": false}\n' > /etc/docker/daemon.json
: > /tmp/tc-bak-names
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do
  python3 -c "import json; p='/etc/docker/daemon.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); d.pop('log-opts', None); d.pop('builder', None); json.dump(d, open(p, 'w'))"
  tc-test-run-component > /tmp/tc-run.out 2>&1 || { echo "change $i failed"; cat /tmp/tc-run.out; exit 1; }
  grep -q 'daemon.json: written' /tmp/tc-run.out || { echo "change $i wrote nothing"; cat /tmp/tc-run.out; exit 1; }
  LC_ALL=C ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* | tail -n 1 >> /tmp/tc-bak-names
done
echo "newest backup after each change:"; sed 's|^/etc/docker/||' /tmp/tc-bak-names
echo "backups after seven changes: $(ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* | wc -l)"
echo "distinct backup names made: $(sort -u /tmp/tc-bak-names | wc -l)"
diff <(LC_ALL=C ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-*) <(LC_ALL=C sort /tmp/tc-bak-names | tail -n 5) && echo "the five left are the newest five"
ls -la /etc/docker
outputContains: the five left are the newest five

steps.label: daemon.json write: an immutable daemon.json (chattr +i; skipped where the filesystem cannot): exit 1, file unchanged, no staging file, no backup
steps.run:
rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker
p=/etc/docker/.tc-immutable-probe; : > $p
if ! chattr +i $p 2>/dev/null || ! lsattr $p 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | grep -q i; then
  chattr -i $p 2>/dev/null; rm -f $p
  echo "SKIPPED: this filesystem does not support chattr +i, so the immutable-file check did not run"; exit 0
fi
chattr -i $p; rm -f $p
f=/etc/docker/daemon.json
printf '%s\n' '{"proxies": {"http-proxy": "http://tc-test-user:tc-test-not-a-password@proxy.invalid:3128"}}' > $f; chmod 600 $f; chattr +i $f
sha256sum $f > /tmp/tc-imm.before
tc-test-run-component > /tmp/tc-imm.out 2>&1; rc=$?
chattr -i $f
cat /tmp/tc-imm.out
echo "component exit: $rc"
ok=0
[ "$rc" = 1 ] || { echo "WRONG: expected exit 1"; ok=1; }
grep -q "could not replace $f" /tmp/tc-imm.out || { echo "WRONG: the output does not say what failed"; ok=1; }
sha256sum -c /tmp/tc-imm.before || { echo "WRONG: daemon.json changed"; ok=1; }
n=$(ls -A /etc/docker | grep -c '^\.daemon\.json\.tc-' || true); echo "staging files left in /etc/docker: $n"; [ "$n" = 0 ] || ok=1
b=$(ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "backups left by the failed run: $b"; [ "$b" = 0 ] || ok=1
ls -la /etc/docker
exit $ok
